key_insight: Clinical prediction model metrics clustered near perfection and at multiples of five and ten, suggesting selective reporting, methodological manipulation, or publication bias.
clinical_relevance: Inflated or incorrectly reported performance could mislead clinicians about prediction models’ usefulness in practice.
method: Examined full texts from a random sample of 2025 Q1 journal articles.
Validated a large language model for data extraction.
Assessed metric clustering and checked reported AUCs against confidence intervals and ROC curves.
evidence_signal: Across 2,001 articles reporting 15,656 AUC values, around 1 in 40 AUCs fell outside their confidence intervals and around 1 in 8 ROC curves did not match the reported AUC.
watch_item: This observational analysis identifies suspicious patterns and reporting inconsistencies but cannot establish intentional manipulation.
paper_title: Clinical Prediction Model Performance Metrics Cluster at Arbitrary Thresholds and are Incorrectly Reported in High-Ranking Journals: An Observational Meta-Research Study
